title: Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Wine Industry: AI-Driven Management in Viticulture, Wine Production and Enotourism
extended_summary:
This paper examines how artificial intelligence could support sustainability and efficiency in the wine industry, focusing on viticulture, wine production, and enotourism in Poland. Rather than testing an AI intervention experimentally, the authors combine a questionnaire survey of winemakers with a literature-based review of AI methods that could be applied to different parts of the wine value chain.

The empirical component is a full-population survey sent to all officially registered active vineyards in Poland; 75 vineyards responded. Respondents reported current sustainability-related practices across environmental, economic, and social dimensions, including reduced pesticide use, renewable energy, waste reuse, local sourcing, community cooperation, and visitor services. The paper then maps these needs to possible AI applications such as drone monitoring, intelligent irrigation, predictive yield systems, production optimization, supply-chain tools, chatbots, recommendation systems, mobile planning tools, and virtual tasting simulations.

The main conclusion is that Polish winemakers already show strong sustainability orientation, and AI could plausibly help them improve resource efficiency, customer engagement, and local economic development. However, the paper is explicitly prospective and conceptual about AI: it does not evaluate a deployed AI system, measure learning outcomes, or compare treatment and control groups. It concludes that AI may be most useful under the current conditions of small-scale Polish vineyards, but successful implementation will depend on tailoring tools to local needs and providing adequate support for adoption.
quality_tier_rationale: The paper is a descriptive survey and conceptual review in viticulture/enotourism, not a peer-reviewed K-12 intervention comparison study. It does not meet credibility criteria for causal evidence on AI-powered tools for scientific reasoning and inquiry in education.
impact_tier_rationale: There is no measurable educational impact reported, and no student learning outcome, effect size, or transfer evidence. Any optimistic thesis about K-12 science AI tools is not supported by this paper; at most, it suggests broad conceptual possibilities for AI in sustainability management outside education.

finding.finding_summary: This paper is not a K-12 causal comparison study and does not report delayed post-tests, transfer tasks, subgroup effects, or implementation-fidelity metrics for student learning. It is a questionnaire-based, descriptive/qualitative study of 75 Polish vineyards (n=75) that proposes AI uses for sustainability, customer engagement, and operational management in wine production and enotourism rather than testing educational outcomes.
finding.measure: Questionnaire responses from winery owners plus thematic coding of open-ended responses; conceptual mapping of AI applications to sustainability domains
